evidence_scope: uncommitted M5 completion tree based on source_commit; durable producer core was previously pushed as b1004c0

profiles: deterministic in-memory RF3 Raft, ISR, and producer state
real RF1 and RF3 segmented WAL close/reopen and truncation fixtures
strict HTTP adapter, bounded Go retry client, real atomic file ledger, and fresh CLI-run recovery

commands.result: all M0 through M5 packages and commands passed
all storage, Raft, replication, producer, HTTP, client, ledger, CLI, model, and subprocess tests passed
all M0 through M5 packages, command tests, and subprocess tests passed under the race detector

acceptance.PR-01: after one committed DATA batch, 100 exact identity/epoch/sequence/digest retries all return offsets [0,0] and the Raft last index never changes
acceptance.PR-02: an RF3 client ignores the original quorum-commit completion, retries the identical batch, receives duplicate=true with the original offsets, and appends no DATA
acceptance.PR-03: a future RF3 leader applies producer state from the committed log, wins a higher-term election after the old leader is isolated, and deduplicates the retry without relying on old-leader RAM; a real RF1 close/reopen fixture provides process-restart replay coverage
acceptance.PR-04: same sequence with different count/digest, sequence gaps, incomplete overlaps, pipelining past an unresolved batch, fenced epochs, and retries older than the 64-result cache return typed errors before append
acceptance.PR-05: the same OpenProducer request_id and parameters survive reply loss and restart without increasing epoch; an explicit new CAS advances exactly once and fences the old epoch
acceptance.PR-06: a real RF3 WAL with committed epoch 0 plus uncommitted DATA and FENCE replays only the committed state; suffix truncation removes provisional LEO without changing epoch or next sequence
acceptance.PR-07: pending-ledger-save, send/reply-loss, broker-success-before-ledger-update, and restart-resume cutpoints preserve the exact request ID, partition, epoch, sequence, and records; a fresh mkfkctl run resumes the durable pending batch before considering new command input
acceptance.OP-01: duplicate-key/unknown-field JSON, invalid base64, unsupported acknowledgements, oversized bodies, and ledger symlink destinations are rejected without reaching the producer backend or reflecting payload bytes
acceptance.OP-04: client retries are bounded by both total deadline and attempt count, keep one pending identity, use jittered capped backoff, and accept NOT_LEADER hints only for broker IDs in the configured static endpoint allowlist

durable_state.truth: FENCE and DATA entries in the committed applied Raft prefix
durable_state.data_binding: producer ID, epoch, first sequence, canonical batch digest, offsets, timestamp, and records share one DATA frame; replay recomputes and verifies the digest
durable_state.speculative_rule: pending operations may reserve memory, but formal epoch/sequence/cache state changes only during committed apply

client_retry.jitter: uniform in the upper half of the current capped exponential backoff
client_retry.ledger_order: save pending and sync before send; save next_sequence and clear pending only after a validated success response

additional_results: Identical pending DATA requests coalesce on one log entry and one acknowledgement gate; conflicting bytes at the same pending sequence return SEQUENCE_CONFLICT.
OpenProducer FENCE entries require Raft quorum commit/apply but do not depend on the user DATA ISR acknowledgement gate.
Cached duplicate retries still capture the current ISR and wait on the existing committed DATA index, preserving M4 acks=all semantics after leader or process restart.
The HTTP adapter reports post-append pending operations as REQUEST_TIMEOUT with outcome=unknown; it never converts timeout into a not-applied claim.
Every M0-M4 storage, Raft, ISR/HW, 100x1000-event, and three-process regression remains in the full gate.
output_location: This scrubbed evidence manifest; no record payloads, producer IDs from users, credentials, ledger contents, or large process artifacts are retained.
limitations: There is not yet a long-running cmd/mkfk broker that wires the HTTP adapter, partition actors, peer transport, metadata endpoint, and lifecycle together; M5 verifies those producer-facing components in-process.
The file ledger is intended for one CLI producer process at a time; callers must not share one ledger path concurrently between processes.
Consumer groups and durable group offsets belong to M6 and do not exist yet.
Idempotence is partition-scoped transport deduplication, not cross-partition transactions or external side-effect exactly-once.
Retention, snapshots, dynamic membership, authentication, and Kafka wire compatibility do not exist.
next_task: M6: implement committed group membership/generation/assignment commands, eager revoke/sync, heartbeat expiry, owner-fenced atomic offset commits, replay, coordinator failover, and group client behavior.
